skills.title: Researching Plants and Soil
skills.description: Put the steps of a research in order. Pick a good question about plants or soil and the best place to find the answer.

skills.title: Fair Tests With Forces
skills.description: Pick the fair test that changes only one thing, like testing how far a ball rolls. Put the steps of an experiment in order.

skills.title: Design, Build, Test Structures
skills.description: Put the steps for designing and building a structure in order. Pick what to change to make it stronger.

skills.title: Safe Investigating
skills.description: Pick the safe way to use tools and materials. Choose the right gear to wear, like gloves for soil.

skills.title: Sharing What We Learned
skills.description: Pick the best way to share your findings with different people. Match science words to what they mean.

skills.title: Test and Fix Code
skills.description: Look at code and pick what it will do. Find the mistake in a program and pick how to fix it.

skills.title: New Technology in Our Lives
skills.description: Pick how coding and new technology change everyday life. Tell the helpful changes from the tricky ones.

skills.title: Science Solves Real Problems
skills.description: Match science and technology at home and in town to the problems they fix. Pick how science works with other subjects to help.

skills.title: Science Ideas From Many People
skills.description: Match science and technology ideas to the communities that gave them to us. Pick how those ideas help.

skills.title: What Plants Need
skills.description: Pick what plants need: air, water, light, heat, nutrients, and space. Pick conditions that can hurt a plant.

skills.title: Parts of a Plant
skills.description: Label the root, stem, leaf, flower, stamen, pistil, seed, cone, and fruit. Pick what each part does for the plant.

skills.title: Plant Life Cycles
skills.description: Put the stages of a plant's life in order, from seed to grown plant. Compare how different plants change.

skills.title: How Plants React and Adapt
skills.description: Match plants to how they react to their home, like leaves turning to the light or dropping in fall.

skills.title: Plants Make Food From Sunlight
skills.description: Pick how plants use sunlight to get energy. They take in carbon dioxide and let out oxygen.

skills.title: How People Use Plants
skills.description: Match plants to how people around the world use them for food, shelter, medicine, and clothing.

skills.title: Plants We Eat
skills.description: Match food plants, including ones grown by First Nations, Métis, and Inuit, to the places they grow or are found.

skills.title: Plants and Animals Need Each Other
skills.description: Pick how plants, animals, and people depend on each other, like plants giving food and animals spreading seeds.

skills.title: Why Plants Matter
skills.description: Pick how plants are important to people and other living things. Pick ways to protect native plants and their homes.

skills.title: People's Actions and Plants
skills.description: Pick how things people do help or hurt plants and their homes. Choose actions you could take to help.

skills.title: Good and Not-So-Good of Local Food
skills.description: Pick the good points and the limits of food grown close to home, like fresher food but a shorter growing season.

skills.title: Contact and Non-Contact Forces
skills.description: Sort forces into ones that touch an object, like pushes and friction, and ones that don't, like gravity and magnets.

skills.title: Ways to Apply a Force
skills.description: Pick how a force is used on an object, like pushing, pulling, twisting, or squeezing.

skills.title: What Forces Do to Objects
skills.description: Pick how forces make an object start, stop, turn, speed up, slow down, or change shape. Compare a big force and a small force.

skills.title: Forces in Daily Life
skills.description: Match everyday jobs, like opening a door or kicking a ball, to the force being used.

skills.title: Forces in Nature and Buildings
skills.description: Pick how wind, water, and gravity affect land and buildings. Pick ways people can lessen or increase these effects.

skills.title: Staying Safe From Forces
skills.description: Pick how forces from things people do can cause harm. Match safety devices, like helmets and seat belts, to how they help.

skills.title: What Is a Structure?
skills.description: Pick what makes a structure: a frame that holds a load and has a size, shape, and job. Sort natural and built structures.

skills.title: Shape Fits the Job
skills.description: Match the shape of a structure to what it is used for, like a wide base on a tower.

skills.title: Strong Structures
skills.description: Pick that strength means holding a load. Pick ways to make a structure or material stronger, like folding or layering.

skills.title: Stable Structures
skills.description: Pick that stability means keeping shape, balance, and staying in place. Pick ways to make a structure steadier, like a wide base.

skills.title: Choosing Building Materials
skills.description: Pick the material properties, like strong, stiff, or waterproof, to think about when building a structure.

skills.title: Forces on Structures
skills.description: Pick how forces like wind, weight, and pushes can change a structure's shape, balance, or place.

skills.title: Struts and Ties
skills.description: Pick which parts of a structure are struts that get pushed together and which are ties that get pulled.

skills.title: Strong Structures and Our World
skills.description: Pick how strong, stable structures, like bridges and dams, help people and affect nature.

skills.title: Animal-Built Structures
skills.description: Compare nests, dams, and hives to human-built structures. Pick how each one affects the environment.

skills.title: What Is in Soil?
skills.description: Sort the living and non-living parts of soil, like worms, roots, sand, and water. Pick what healthy soil is like.

skills.title: What Gets Added to Soil
skills.description: Pick things added to soil, like fertilizer, compost, salt, and pollution. Pick how each one affects soil health.

skills.title: Soil Types in Ontario
skills.description: Match Ontario soils, like sandy, clay, and loam, to the crops and foods they grow well.

skills.title: Erosion
skills.description: Put the steps of erosion in order. Pick what causes it, like wind and water, and how it harms soil.

skills.title: Keeping Soil Healthy
skills.description: Pick ways farmers and gardeners in Ontario keep soil healthy, like cover crops and rotating crops.

skills.title: Composting
skills.description: Put the steps of composting in order. Sort what can be composted and pick how compost helps soil.

skills.title: Why Soil Matters
skills.description: Pick how soil helps people, plants, and animals, like growing food and giving homes to animals.

skills.title: People's Actions and Soil
skills.description: Pick how things people do, like building and farming, hurt or help soil. Pick ways to protect it.
